summary: Extends the RTP payload format for uncompressed studio-quality video from RFC 4175 to support additional color sampling modes. It is standards-track.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC adds six ways to describe colour sampling for uncompressed video over RTP. The plus sign identifies which colour component uses one more bit than the others.

how to signal 16 bit rgb video in sdp
what are the rtp uncompressed video sampling modes

subtitle: Six colour-sampling modes for signalling uncompressed video with uneven component depths.

tldr.problem: The uncompressed RTP video format could carry RGB video with uneven component depths but could not signal it using the existing parameters.
tldr.mechanism: Six new sampling values mark which colour component receives one extra bit beyond the depth parameter.
tldr.outcome: The extension allows formats such as 5-bit red, 6-bit green, and 5-bit blue to be signalled; it updates RFC 4175.

today: RFC 4421 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 4175. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes it.

sections.title: The Signalling Gap
sections.content:
RFC 4175 defines an RTP payload format for uncompressed, studio-quality video and parameters for image size, colour space, pixel depth, and sampling. Its signalling assumes the same number of bits per sample for every colour component.

That could describe RGB with equal component depths, but not a format with different depths for red, green, and blue, even though the payload format could carry it.
sections.plainLanguage: The existing settings could describe equal detail for each colour. They could not describe a format that gives one colour an extra bit.

sections.title: The Six Sampling Modes
sections.content:
The new values are RGB+, RG+B, R+GB, BGR+, BG+R, and B+GR. They use the packing order of the corresponding RGB or BGR mode, except the component marked with a plus MUST use one extra bit.

The mandatory parameter depth=N gives N bits to unmarked components and N+1 bits to the marked one. The memo highlights depth 5 as a common case in which a pixel fits into two octets without padding.
sections.plainLanguage: The plus sign shows which colour gets an extra bit. The depth value tells how many bits the other colours use.

sections.title: Example and Security
sections.content:
The example signals a format with 5-bit red and blue components and a 6-bit green component using sampling=RG+B and depth=5. It also gives image dimensions and other SDP parameters.

The IANA section adds the six values to the sampling parameter of the video/raw media type. The security considerations of RFC 4175 apply; this extension adds none.
sections.plainLanguage: The example uses RG+B to mark green as the component with extra detail. The RFC adds the sampling value to the registered list.
